cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Miao/Guizhou (Southwest Chinese minority) baby-carrier — the T-shaped silk-embroidered panel in red/orange/pink on black cotton, paired with indigo-and-white resist-dyed straps, is a distinctive, well-known Miao textile form, not Javanese batik or embroidery tradition.

physical.title: baby-carrier
physical.summary: Baby-carrier in form of funnel-shaped cotton cloth. The main design is T-shaped, with an inner pattern of angular forms in squares and lozenges, embroidered in red, pink and orange silk on a black dyed cotton base bordered by narrow bands of plain colour, triangles or small squares and oblongs. Below the main design are several horizontal bands, also embroidered in silk of the same colours as the main design, but with some blue thread in addition. The whole piece is bordered with a band of white, machine-woven cotton along the middle of which a narrower band of blue cotton has been added by appliqué; the white and blue strips towards the bottom of the piece are brighter than elsewhere, and all these outer strips are machine-sewn. The cloth is backed by one large blue-dyed piece of cotton and at the bottom by a smaller piece of finer, black-dyed cotton. For tying, two lengths of white-on-blue cotton batik are machine-sewn towards the top of the cloth, one each side.

cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-drawn batik kemben (breast-cloth) with soga and indigo dyeing, tritik and lidah api motifs — a textile form and technique characteristic of Javanese dress.

physical.title: breast-cloth
physical.summary: A woman's cotton (tabby) batik breast-cloth, a 'kemben'; hand-drawn on both sides.  Dyed in soga (brown) and indigo.  Rectangular blue panel in centre echoed in ever-widening bands.  The central panel is edged with 'tritik' (sewn tie-dye) pattern.  Surrounding this panel is a row of inward-pointing flame ('lidah api') motifs.  Those on the long sides sloping towards the middle of the cloth, in black and soga against a cream ground, within a rectangular border of spade shapes, alternately pointing up or down.  Outside this is a narrow border of wavy lines in white dots against a blue ground.  Narrow 'sisir' strips along long sides and short ends, outside an inner border of more complex narrower sisir stripes.  Star design at each corner.  Veining produced by 'remukkan process', in which the wax has been deliberately cracked to allow the dye to seep through, in the 'lidah api' and spade pattern sections. Hemmed on one long side and both short ends. Small area of damage at one corner.   [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]
